x: Grieve, of the School, once again won both sprints, although young Peter Vine was a good runner-up in both races, and this finely-built young man should prove a good addition to our sprinting strength.

Metcalfe took the furlong in 23.6s., being chased home by Brant, Harris, Molyneux and Vine. Watts scored a double by winning the 440 in 51.1s., with Bishop third, and 880 in 2m. 5.4s., with Brown third and Bishop fourth.
The 100 Yards, won in 10.1s., saw Peter Vine about a yard away with Hayes fourth. Peter stepped into the breach and tackled the quarter, and was a good third in 54.1.
High Jump: 1 Jones (B.), 4 ft. 11 ins.; 2 Fleming (B.), 4ft. 10 ins.; 3 Vine (B.), 4 ft. 9 ins. Long Jump: 1 Jones (B.), 18 ft. 7 ins.; 2 Fleming (B.), 17 ft. 8 ins.

Dennis Merrett was most unlucky to come up against two hurdlers (Vine and Shaw) at the peak of their form and although his time of 24.7 secs. was a little slower than his Southern Championship record made a few weeks earlier, his performance was nevertheless of a very high standard.
